The full loop runs on-chain

An observation attested by ~100 FDC data providers, an allocation decided inside
the enclave, and a rebalance executed through every guardrail:

  attested price   : $1.022211
  attested volume  : $720,363,840
  change 1h/6h/24h : -0.28% / -0.81% / -1.97%
  targets          : [948, 2287, 0]  (mixed conditions; partial deployment)
  status           : SUCCESS

tx 0xa3153a9b722377a46b2e8155120c2cd392b5cba494a2adf8d3da22ea1b977301

Readable back off the chain: rebalanceNonce() is 1, lastSignal() returns
(1022211, 720363840, -28, -81, -197), and lastFtsoPriceMicroUsd() is 1022162 —
0.48 basis points from the attested price, well inside the 5% band the vault
enforced before accepting the plan.

The enclave read a market under mild stress and deployed 32% of the vault rather
than its 90% maximum. That judgement is its own; the vault's only opinion was
that it was permitted.

Diagnosing the first failed attempt is worth recording. It reverted with empty
returndata, which Coston2's RPC reports as a bare "execution reverted" and which
a fork replay confirmed carried no error data at all. The cause was that the
deployed bytecode predated the signal reshape, so abi.decode was reading a
five-field payload into a seven-field struct — a length mismatch reverts with no
data, which is why no custom error appeared. Redeploying against current source
fixed it.

README and Todo corrected: they described the loop as not yet working.
Point UI and docs at the reshaped signal and the current deployment

Reshape the signal around a source the FDC providers actually attest

The pipeline was blocked on Bitstamp, which the verifier accepts and the data
providers will not fetch. Coinpaprika attests and is the only attesting source
carrying price, volume and several return horizons in one document, so the
signal DTO is now shaped around what is actually obtainable rather than what
would have been convenient.

MarketSignal is now {price, 24h volume, 1h/6h/24h returns}. Three horizons turn
out to be a better volatility input than the high-low range they replace: the
shape of recent movement carries more information than its extent, and a market
that round-tripped 2% in an hour should not be treated like one that drifted 2%
over a day. Returns are scaled by sqrt(time) to a common 24h basis and the worst
horizon sizes the position, because volatility is a risk measure.

Freshness no longer comes from a timestamp in the payload. It is derived from
the attestation's own voting round — the chain's record of when ~100 providers
agreed on the observation, which a compromised endpoint cannot backdate. A
source-supplied timestamp was only ever a claim by the source.

Coinpaprika returns JSON numbers rather than strings, so the jq needs tostring
first; appending ".0" before splitting keeps integer-valued fields from making
.[1] null and blowing up the filter.

Conformance vector regenerated from a live enclave run. Two Foundry ordering
traps fixed along the way: a proof helper that read state issued a non-reverting
call after vm.expectRevert was armed, and the stale-signal tests ran at
timestamp 1 — before the voting-epoch origin — where every round is in the
future and nothing can ever read as stale.

61 Solidity + 10 Go tests.

Make the vault standards-conformant, and document how it is used

Standards work. The vault claimed to be an ERC-4626 product but was missing the
conventions an integrator assumes are present, and one of the gaps was a real
security bug rather than a formality:

- Every ERC-4626 entry point is now nonReentrant. OpenZeppelin's ERC4626 is
  unguarded, which is correct for a vault that holds its own assets and wrong
  for one that does not: _withdraw calls into venue contracts — foreign code —
  before super._withdraw burns shares, so a hostile venue could re-enter while
  the caller's shares still existed.
- ERC-165 supportsInterface, so integrators can discover the vault on-chain.
- Ownable2Step, so a mistyped address cannot orphan the vault.
- Pausable, with a deliberate asymmetry: pausing stops deposits and rebalances
  and never stops withdrawals. An operator who can freeze exits can rug.
- maxDeposit/maxMint report the pause, as ERC-4626 requires.

StandardsCompliance.t.sol covers all of it (9 tests). The reentrancy test
initially passed with the guard removed — the reentrant call happened to fail
on liquidity instead — so it now asserts the ReentrancyGuard selector
specifically, verified by mutation.

Redeployed, because the previous address predated the hardening and the
documentation would otherwise have described a contract that was not the one
deployed. Every claim in Explanation.md is checked against the live vault.

Explanation.md is new: a user-facing guide covering depositors, integrators,
relayers and operators, what is being trusted and what is not, how to read the
vault's state independently, and what each error message means.

Also fixed: the UI silently ran against the previous deployment because ES
modules and deployments.json are cached per-origin and survive tab closes,
which presents a dead vault as an empty one.

Review pass: fix stale references and overstated claims

demo.sh had been broken since the Tacit rename — it still invoked
offchain/signal.py, which is now signal_source.py. Caught by actually running
it end to end rather than assuming.

The README described Bitstamp as the working signal source in the architecture
diagram, the lifecycle and the FDC section. Bitstamp validates at the verifier
and is never attested by the providers, so a judge following those instructions
would have hit exactly the wall we hit. Those sections now describe the real
state, and Limitations names the gap outright instead of implying the loop runs.

signal_source.py carries the same warning at the top, with the attesting and
non-attesting host lists and why switching is a DTO change rather than a URL
swap.

UI: venue reads were sequential and issued twice per refresh, so the allocation
panel sat on a placeholder for several seconds while every other figure was
live. They are now batched and cached, and the placeholder says it is loading
rather than asking for a wallet connection it does not need.

Map which market-data hosts FDC providers will attest

Five candidates submitted in one round. Gemini, Coinbase and Coinpaprika are
attested; Bitstamp and api.exchange.coinbase.com are not — the distinction is
per-host and unpredictable, since api.coinbase.com works while
api.exchange.coinbase.com does not.

Gemini is the best fit: open/high/low/close come back as strings, which suits
the verifier's floor-less jq subset. A Gemini filter validates VALID.
Update Todo with de-risked relayer status

Diagnose FDC attestation: fee contract, and verifier vs provider reachability

Two findings from getting the rebalance loop working against live Coston2.

The request fee is not on FdcHub — FdcHub.getRequestFee reverts, and the fee
lives on FdcRequestFeeConfigurations. Underpaying reverts with a message naming
a method the hub does not expose, which sends you to the wrong contract.

More importantly: the verifier and the data providers are different machines.
prepareRequest returning VALID proves only that the verifier could reach a URL.
A request can be VALID, submitted and paid for, then silently never attested,
with the DA layer answering "attestation request not found" indefinitely —
indistinguishable from a round that has not finalised.

A controlled experiment with a known-good control copied from Flare's own
FdcTrafficMaker confirms it: jsonplaceholder attests, Bitstamp does not, in
either parameter shape.

Consequences:
- fdc.py now separates "not finalised" from "not attested" and fails loudly
- probe_attestation.py / probe_sources.py isolate which hosts providers accept
- verify_real_proof.py validates our proof handling against a real finalised
  Coston2 attestation, independent of our own source being attested. It returns
  true, so tuple encoding, Merkle handling and payload decoding are confirmed
  correct against production data.

Tacit: confidential autonomous FXRP treasury on Flare

An ERC-4626 FXRP vault whose allocation is decided by a strategy running inside
a Flare Confidential Compute enclave, and whose safety does not depend on that
enclave being honest.

The contribution is the trust boundary. Five invariants — conservation, venue
caps, turnover, an FTSO price band and FDC signal binding — bound what a fully
authenticated enclave can do, so the enclave controls strategy quality and never
fund safety.

Flare integration, all load-bearing:
- FCC runs the allocation model; weights never leave the enclave
- FDC Web2Json attests the market observation each plan is bound to
- FTSO bounds the reference price the enclave claims to have used
- FXRP is the managed asset, resolved from AssetManagerFXRP.fAsset()

Notable findings, documented rather than left as folklore:
- abi.encodePacked pads ARRAY elements to 32 bytes; the Go signer originally
  packed 2 bytes per uint16 and produced valid signatures over the wrong bytes
- the FDC verifier runs a restricted jq subset (no floor/round/sub/ltrimstr)
  and most crypto APIs are unreachable from it
- Firelight stXRP settles withdrawals asynchronously behind a synchronous
  ERC-4626 interface, burning shares without paying; the adapter now refuses
  rather than booking phantom losses

51 Solidity tests including a malicious-enclave invariant campaign and fork
tests against live third-party bytecode, plus 8 Go tests.
